A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ap3b1 and Hps1 genes regulate the melanosome biogenesis in the neural crest cells and the tyrosinase transport in the RPE differently.
the hypopigmation in eyes of pearl mouse was due to the defect of tyrosinase trafficking in melanocytes, while the defect in melanosome biogenesis was not a primary cause.

the hypopignentation in iris of pearl mice is more severe than pale eye mice due to the aberrantly transported tyrsinase in melanocytes, while the macromelanosomal accumulation in melanocytes and increased lipofuscin accumulation in RPE are not present in pearl mice, suggesting that HPS-2 and HPS-1 have different effects on melanin production and melanosome biogenesis in melanocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ap3b1 mutant mouse is a better model for studying the pathogenesis of human Hermansky-Podlalk syndrome 2.
the Ap3b1 mutation in eyes of pearl mouse causes the hypopigmentations of the iris and choroidal stroma, but does not affect the pigmentation of neural crest-derived melanophores in eyes.
